scoreRule: 1 point per correct MC item; 10 points maximum; local provisional grade only
description: Original EN/B1 Email Friend test bank for independent reading; pedagogical approval pending.

tabs.title: Understanding the message
tabs.description: Interpret the writer's purpose and feelings.

tabs.title: Responding appropriately
tabs.description: Choose a response supported by the message.

questions.q: Why does the changed town square remind Tomas to contact Robin?
choices: He wants Robin to complain about the changes to the council.
He has heard that Robin will move back next week.
The shop has started selling the same football boots as before.
Seeing the new workshop makes him think of their shared past and lost contact.
questions.explanation: The transformation prompts memories and the realisation that the friends have barely spoken.

questions.q: What does Tomas learn from helping younger children at the workshop?
choices: Volunteer work is useful only when it earns money.
Even someone still learning can make a useful contribution.
It is essential to be a professional before offering help.
Children can teach adults to repair bicycle lights.
questions.explanation: The children treat Tomas like an expert, but he reflects that help need not require expertise.

questions.q: What does the collection of old photographs contribute to the workshop?
choices: It connects people with different periods of the neighbourhood's history.
It shows that the present-day square has not changed.
It mainly advertises tools that people can borrow.
It replaces the need for older volunteers.
questions.explanation: The photographs and Mrs Okafor's stories preserve memories of the former square.

questions.q: Why does Tomas say Robin need not prepare a speech for the open day?
choices: The organisers have cancelled all planned activities.
He hopes Robin will bring no photographs.
He wants the invitation to feel relaxed and easy to accept.
He knows Robin dislikes speaking in every situation.
questions.explanation: Tomas removes expectations so even a brief appearance is welcome.

questions.q: Why does Tomas describe his small first tasks at the workshop?
choices: He thinks carrying boxes is more important than repairing objects.
He is disappointed that he was not trusted with difficult repairs at first.
He wants Robin to know that making tea is the main goal.
They help show how he moved from feeling nervous to participating confidently.
questions.explanation: His early nervousness contrasts with later teaching younger children.

questions.q: What does Tomas's memory of Robin's photographs help explain?
choices: He thinks Robin's hobby could make a meaningful contribution to the open day.
He wants Robin to pay for a professional photographer.
He expects Robin to organise all the workshop activities.
He needs photographs of other towns for the wall.
questions.explanation: Tomas associates Robin with photographs of everyday life and invites that interest into the event.

questions.q: Why does Tomas offer travel alternatives instead of insisting on the open day?
choices: Robin is not allowed to visit the old neighbourhood.
He recognises the time and expense involved and values keeping in contact anyway.
He prefers speaking on a screen to meeting in person.
He has decided to stop volunteering at the workshop.
questions.explanation: Tomas offers to travel himself or arrange a call and says Robin should not feel guilty.

questions.q: A nervous newcomer wants to help a community project but has few skills. What would Tomas's experience suggest?
choices: Take on the hardest job to prove they belong.
Wait until another volunteer asks for money.
Start with manageable tasks and learn while contributing.
Avoid helping anyone until they earn a qualification.
questions.explanation: Tomas begins with small tasks and gains confidence and useful skills.

questions.q: Robin cannot afford the journey home. Which action best fits the tone of Tomas's email?
choices: Ask Tomas to cancel the open day.
Promise to attend despite the travel cost.
Accept a video call or suggest meeting during the holidays.
Stop replying because the invitation cannot be accepted.
questions.explanation: Tomas explicitly offers calls and a different visit because he values their relationship.

questions.q: What would be the most constructive response to Tomas's closing question?
choices: Suggest waiting another year until there is a special occasion.
Propose a simple regular conversation rather than waiting for a major event.
Tell him that only a large event justifies keeping in contact.
Send only a reaction to the latest social-media picture.
questions.explanation: Tomas closes by asking that they stop treating special occasions as a condition for speaking.
